issues.claim: Sources line: https://www.neifund.org/hollanderelectric-llc/ — preventive-maintenance programme for industrial facilities (supporting Section 3: 'public pages show switchgear, motor controls, standby generators and an industrial maintenance programme').
issues.problem: The cited URL does not exist. It returns HTTP 404 with the page title 'Page not found | NEIF' (and is marked noindex). Opening it and searching its text returns no mention of 'maintenance', 'preventive' or 'industrial'. So the only source given for this claim is dead and does not support it. The underlying claim is nonetheless true, but it is supported by the business's own homepage, not by NEIF.
issues.fix: Replace the NEIF URL with https://hollanderelectric.com/, which states 'Preventive maintenance programs' and '24/7 emergency industrial response' under Industrial Electrical. If the NEIF contractor-listing point is wanted (JCP&L/financing angle), find and cite the live NEIF page before using it, or drop it.

issues.claim: Sources line: 'https://api.bls.gov/publicAPI/v1/timeseries/data/OEUS340000000000043405113 — BLS OEWS New Jersey medians used for the wage lines (customer-service rep $47,740; dispatcher $54,590; electrician median $77,250, May 2025).'
issues.problem: One series URL is cited for three figures, but that series is occupation 43-4051 only and contains only the value 47740. The dispatcher ($54,590) and electrician ($77,250) medians are not in the cited response, so two of the three wage lines are not traceable to the URL given. The figures themselves are correct (verified against their own series).
issues.fix: Cite all three series separately: OEUS340000000000043405113 ($47,740 CSR, already correct), OEUS340000000000043503213 ($54,590 dispatcher) and OEUS340000000000047211113 ($77,250 electrician).

issues.problem: Minor. The name comes only from the published business mailbox toby@hollanderelectric.com; no page states Toby's role. The draft does hedge this with 'confirm the right person before sending', so it is not presented as certain, but the greeting itself reads as a stated identity.
issues.fix: Keep the hedge, and consider 'Hi Toby' -> 'Hi —' or 'Hello Hollander Electric team' if the first email may reach a shared inbox, or retain 'Hi Toby' only after the visit confirms the role.
